This may be intrinsic to me, but whenever I got advice from parents (prior to my son being born) it was tough for me to hear because I just figured: "No biggie, I got it." Then, enter those first few months...Anyhow, things were much easier with our 2nd child. I was curious if this was true for some of the other parents or, potentially, was their advice you received you wish you hadn't taken? Personally, I wish my pre-child self could have appreciated my mother's warning: "Sleep deprivation is a real thing."
Basic Question: Parents that are a year in, what advice do you wish you'd listened to? Or, alternately, what was the worst advice you got?

I just wish somebody, anybody, or one of the books I read, one of the videos I watched, or one of the classes I took, had clued me in that the first 6 months might be objectively unpleasant to live through. Everybody says congrats, and everyone wishes you well, but you're left to discover the struggles of reality on your own. Most parents quickly learn, as they encounter challenges, that lots of parents they've known also endured some of the frequent difficulties associated with caring for infants: sleep deprivation, the stress of frequent crying, a serious strain on the relationship and their sex lives, but very few, I think, got much in terms of an advanced warning.mmaybe people just don't want to be gloomy on the eve of a new life entering the world, but I wish somebody had given me a head's up that the transition to parent might register as one of the hardest things I'd ever do. I think that would have made it less traumatic.

I think this comes from people being worried that by recognizing the frustration they are being negative about having children or, perhaps, not being tough enough. I recall a lot of joke-y stuff like "So, getting any sleep huh?"just after our son was born and being incredibly annoyed. In retrospect, I suppose it was kind of intended as an inside-joke amongst Club Parent. Like you said, we've all had to face these issues. I know for a long time I just felt incredibly guilty, until I could just accept the stress of newborns as normal.

  • 1/2 cup soy sauce
  • 5 cloves garlic, crushed
  • 1 tablespoon black peppercorns
  • 5 bay leaves

Add the chicken and all ingredients.

Close and lock the lid, cook 15 minutes for Electirc and 12 Minutes for Stovetop, use natural relese.
